title: Redwood discovery - Sentinel AI latency & throughput
summary: Initial latency and throughput discovery with Sentinel AI. Main goals: p95 latency under 300ms for short-form streaming responses, sustained concurrency target 200 users (~50 concurrent requests), batch token/sec benchmarking for long-form generation. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, KV/prefix caching, and security requirements (SSO, SOC2, KMS). Action items: run a token/sec benchmark with a 2k prompt, share security pack, schedule dedicated capacity sizing call.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs and SOC2 summary (Jordan)
SE to run a 2k-token benchmark on Redwood hosted and share results (Maya)
Schedule dedicated sizing call w/ infra team (all) - proposed 2026-04-01
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send security docs + SOC2 summary (due 2026-03-27)
Maya Patel: Run token/sec + latency bench (2k prompt, streaming and non-streaming) on hosted and dedicated variants (due 2026-03-30)
Carlos Mendez: Share example traffic profile and p95 SLA targets (due 2026-03-28)
transcript:
Date/time: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE); Maya (Redwood SE); Carlos (Sentinel, Head of ML); Priya (SRE); Liam (CTO)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
00:08 Carlos: Yeah hi, Carlos here, head of ML at Sentinel. We're focused on realtime agent responses for our monitoring product.
00:16 Liam: Liam, CTO, keen to understand infra impact.
00:20 Priya: Priya, SRE, I'll be focusing on networking, VPC, and security constraints.
00:28 Jordan: Great. Maya from our SE team will walk through latency/throughput questions. Maya?
00:34 Maya: Hey all. Quick agenda, we'll cover p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, then benchmarking plan.
01:00 Maya: To start, can you give a sense of current traffic? what's your p95 targets, concurrent users, typical prompt lengths?
01:12 Carlos: Sure. We've got a realtime alerting flow where users type a one-line prompt and get a streamed answer. Target p95 for first token ideally < 250-300ms, but for full response we expect about 1-2s for short answers. For longer doc generation we want throughput - about 2k tokens at scale, and batch throughput matter.
01:35 Maya: Okay, and concurrent?
01:37 Carlos: Our product peak is around 200 active users and we're sizing for about 50 concurrent inference requests (avg). Bursts up to 150 concurrent.
01:45 Jordan: So p95 for short streaming is the primary SLO, and then token/sec for long-running jobs.
02:00 Priya: Also, we need to know hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, especially on data residency and VPC peering. SOC2 obviously.
02:10 Maya: We'll get to that. For latency we typically see two components: network+transport and model compute. For streaming first-token latency usually dominated by model load and kv cache warmup if not cached.
02:28 Maya: Do you have model family in mind? open models or proprietary?
02:32 Carlos: Mostly open models, something like Llama-3 variants, and some finetuned smaller models.
02:38 Maya: Good. A couple notes: Hosted will give fastest time-to-value but shared capacity means noisy neighbors sometimes add jitter. Dedicated gives predictable p95 and throughput but needs a committed pool. Private gives full control but adds ops overhead.
03:00 Liam: For predictable p95 we lean dedicated but want to validate cost tradeoff. What's the typical tokens/sec on a 2k prompt for a 7B vs 33B model in Redwood?
03:12 Maya: Rough numbers — on A100-class dedicated instances with our runtime, a quantized 7B can do ~1,200-2,000 tokens/sec depending on batch and batching profile; 33B ~200-400 tokens/sec. But these range widely with sequence length and kv caching.
03:30 Carlos: That 1,200-2k tokens/sec for 7B seems optimistic; what's the p95 per-token latency at small batch=1 streaming?
03:38 Maya: Per-token 1-2 ms at runtime if KV/resident in GPU, but end-to-end first-token is often 100-300ms due to tokenization, request routing, and small-model cold starts. Streaming adds per-chunk overhead.
03:55 Priya: Network wise, we have an egress constraint and prefer VPC peering for private deployments. In hosted, what guarantees do you have for regional placement?
04:06 Jordan: Hosted lets you pin region and we have routing policies; dedicated gives dedicated regional pools. For Private, that's fully customer-managed.
04:20 Carlos: Benchmarks — can you run a p95/throughput run with our prompt set? We'll share prompts.
04:24 Maya: Yes, we'll run token/sec and p95 for both hosted and a dedicated-style config (simulate dedicated by isolating workload). We'll include streaming measurements (first-byte p95, and end-to-end completion p95).
04:40 Liam: Also need to know concurrency scaling characteristics. If we go from 50 to 150 concurrent requests what's expected latency tail behavior?
04:48 Maya: For concurrency, two levers: autoscaling + batching. For low-latency SLOs we keep batch sizes small and scale pods; for cost we let batching increase. We can provide recommended autoscale policies. Expect roughly linear degradation as you saturate GPU; p95 can jump significantly beyond saturation.
05:10 Carlos: Any specific metrics you measure? token/s per GPU, p95-first-byte, p95-completion, queueing time, batch size distribution?
05:18 Maya: Yes — we capture token/sec per-GPU, p50/p95/p99 latency for first-byte and completion, batch sizes, queue time, and GPU utilization. We'll share sample dashboards.
05:30 Jordan: On security, Priya, anything special?
05:33 Priya: We need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS for key management, and SOC2. Also data residency in eu-west for certain customers.
05:45 Jordan: We have those — SOC2 report and KMS integrations. We'll send security pack.
05:50 Carlos: For the benchmark, can you simulate 50 concurrent short streaming requests and 10 concurrent long 2k token jobs simultaneously? That mixes real-world load.
05:59 Maya: Yes that mix is helpful. We'll run both streaming-first-byte p95 and long-run token/sec. We'll include both quantized and fp16 runs.
06:12 Liam: Curious about prefix/KV cache behavior for multi-turn chat. If cache warmup affects cold-start latency a lot, can we pre-warm?
06:22 Maya: We support pre-warming and persistent KV caches for dedicated/private. Hosted can do warmed pools for active models at an increased cost.
06:34 Carlos: Any multitenant isolation concerns? We want deterministic p95.
06:38 Maya: Dedicated removes noisy neighbors; we also enforce tenant scheduling and capacity reservations.
06:45 Priya: About VPC peering — how is mTLS or encryption in transit handled?
06:51 Jordan: mTLS is supported for Private and Dedicated peering. Hosted uses TLS and regional routing, plus optional private endpoints.
07:00 Carlos: Ok people — let's recap next steps.
07:04 Jordan: Recap: Redwood will run benches (Maya), send security docs (Jordan), Sentinel will share prompts and traffic profile (Carlos). We'll schedule dedicated sizing follow-up.
07:15 Priya: Can we get an example infra diagram?
07:18 Jordan: We'll attach a network diagram in the security pack.
07:22 Liam: Target timeline? We want a pilot in 4 weeks.
07:25 Jordan: Sounds doable. We'll aim benches in 5 business days, security pack within 48 hours.
07:30 Carlos: Great. Thanks all.
07:33 Jordan: Thanks, meeting ends.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "kv cache" transcribed as "k v cache" at times, "A100" rendered as "A ten A" in one segment. Some speaker overlaps and brief crosstalk.
